mainTopic: Why the משנה forbids immersing one vessel inside another for קודש: רבי אילא says the reason is חציצה, while רבא says it is a separate גזירה about narrow-mouthed vessels.
overview: The amud opens at the end of a צריכא. According to רבי אילא, both the vessel-inside-a-vessel case and the knot case are about חציצה, and the גמרא explains why the משנה still needed to teach both. It then shows that רבי אילא is consistent with his teaching, in the name of רבי חנינא בר פפא, that the משנה lists only ten מעלות. That count works because he treats these two cases as one. The first five מעלות also apply to חולין שנעשו על טהרת הקודש, but the last five apply only to real קודש. The reason is that the first five are linked to Torah-level טומאה and the last five are purely rabbinic. רבא disagrees: since the סיפא is the חציצה rule, the רישא must have another reason. He says it is a גזירה so that people will not immerse needles inside a vessel whose mouth is narrower than the tube of a wineskin. He backs this measure with a משנה about joining מקוואות, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Why the משנה needed both the knot case and the vessel-in-vessel case
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes explaining why both cases are needed. From the knot case alone, we might have thought that a vessel floating in water is not a חציצה.
steps.simpleTranslation: A knot gets tighter in water, so it clearly blocks the water. In the first case, the water lifts the top vessel so it floats. We might have said that is no blocking at all. So both cases had to be taught.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing its answer to the question of why the משנה taught two cases that both seem to be about חציצה. The answer is that each case teaches something the other does not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the משנה had taught only the knot case, we would think it is a חציצה only because water makes knots tighter. With one vessel inside another, the water makes the top vessel float, so we might think nothing presses down and blocks the water. That is why the first case also had to be taught.

keyTerms.meaning: Something blocking the water from touching the item being immersed
It is necessary (both cases had to be taught)

phrases.english: that a knot in water gets pulled even tighter,
but in the first clause,
phrases.notes: The first case in the משנה is immersing one vessel inside another.

phrases.english: where the water makes the vessel float —
I would have said it is not a blocking,
so it is necessary to teach both.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the צריכא answer that began on the previous part of the daf.
steps.terutzResolutionType: צריכא: each case teaches something the other could not
steps.terutzHavaAmina: From the knot case alone, we might think a floating vessel inside another vessel is not a חציצה.
steps.terutzMaskana: Both cases count as חציצה, so the משנה needed to state both.

steps.title: רבי אילא is consistent: the משנה lists only ten stringencies
steps.stepSummary: רבי אילא, quoting רבי חנינא בר פפא, says the משנה teaches ten מעלות. The first five apply even to חולין prepared in the purity of קודש, and the last five apply only to real קודש.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אילא is following his own approach. He said in the name of רבי חנינא בר פפא that the משנה lists ten extra stringencies. The first five apply to קודש and also to ordinary food prepared in the purity of קודש. The last five apply only to קודש itself.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that רבי אילא's view here fits another teaching of his. He counts ten מעלות in the משנה, not eleven.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה seems to list eleven cases. רבי אילא counts only ten, so he must be joining two of them into one. That fits his view that the vessel-in-vessel case and the knot case share one reason, חציצה.

keyTerms.meaning: Extra stringencies (here, ones that apply to קודש)
Ordinary food that a person chose to prepare in the purity standard of קודש

steps.confusionAlert: The number ten matters. The משנה seems to have eleven cases, and counting ten shows that רבי אילא treats two of them as a single stringency.

phrases.english: Rabbi Ila follows his own reasoning,
for Rabbi Ila said
that Rabbi Ḥanina bar Pappa said:
They taught ten stringencies here,
phrases.notes: "Here" is our משנה. It seems to list eleven, so he must be counting two of them as one.

phrases.english: the first five apply both to sacrificial food

phrases.aramaic: בֵּין לְחוּלִּין שֶׁנַּעֲשׂוּ עַל טׇהֳרַת הַקֹּדֶשׁ,
phrases.english: and to ordinary food prepared in the purity of sacrificial food,
the last five apply to sacrificial food,

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל לֹא לְחוּלִּין שֶׁנַּעֲשׂוּ עַל טׇהֳרַת הַקֹּדֶשׁ.
phrases.english: but not to ordinary food prepared in the purity of sacrificial food.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אִילָא לְטַעְמֵיהּ, דְּאָמַר רַבִּי אִילָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows that רבי אילא's approach, which ties the two cases together, matches his count of ten מעלות.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: There are ten מעלות in the משנה. The first five also apply to חולין שנעשו על טהרת הקודש, and the last five apply only to קודש.

steps.title: Why are the first five different from the last five?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the first five מעלות and the last five are treated differently.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sets up the next move by asking why רבי אילא splits the ten stringencies into two groups.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אילא gave a rule but no reason for it. The גמרא wants to know why the first five reach חולין prepared in the purity of קודש while the last five do not.

phrases.english: What is the reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind the split in step 2.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why only the first five מעלות apply to חולין שנעשו על טהרת הקודש.

steps.title: The first five are connected to Torah-level impurity
steps.stepSummary: The first five have a link to טומאה מדאורייתא, so the רבנן applied them more widely. The last five have no such link, so the רבנן limited them to real קודש.
steps.simpleTranslation: The first five are connected to impurity from the Torah, so the רבנן made them apply to both קודש and ordinary food prepared in the purity of קודש. The last five have no Torah-level connection, so the רבנן made them apply only to קודש and not to that ordinary food.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its question. How widely a stringency applies depends on whether it is connected to Torah-level impurity.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first five could lead to real טומאה מדאורייתא, so the רבנן were stricter and included ordinary food kept in the purity of קודש. The last five rest only on rabbinic impurity, so the רבנן kept them for real קודש alone.

keyTerms.meaning: A connection or link to impurity
The first ones / the last ones

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי אילא, the first five מעלות are linked to Torah-level impurity, so they apply even to חולין שנעשו על טהרת הקודש. The last five are purely rabbinic and apply only to קודש.

phrases.aramaic: חֲמֵשׁ קַמָּיָיתָא, דְּאִית לְהוּ דְּרָרָא דְטוּמְאָה מִדְּאוֹרָיְיתָא —
phrases.english: The first five, which have a connection to impurity from Torah law —
the Sages decreed them

phrases.aramaic: בֵּין לְקֹדֶשׁ בֵּין לְחוּלִּין שֶׁנַּעֲשׂוּ עַל טׇהֳרַת הַקֹּדֶשׁ,
phrases.english: both for sacrificial food and for ordinary food prepared in the purity of sacrificial food,

phrases.aramaic: בָּתְרָיָיתָא, דְּלֵית לְהוּ דְּרָרָא דְטוּמְאָה מִדְּאוֹרָיְיתָא —
phrases.english: the last ones, which have no connection to impurity from Torah law —
the Sages decreed them for sacrificial food,
but for ordinary food prepared in the purity of sacrificial food —
the Sages did not decree them.

steps.triggerLanguage: חֲמֵשׁ קַמָּיָיתָא, דְּאִית לְהוּ דְּרָרָא דְטוּמְאָה מִדְּאוֹרָיְיתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question asked in step 3.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The first five are linked to טומאה מדאורייתא, so they were decreed more widely. The last five are not, so they were limited to קודש.

steps.title: רבא: the first clause is not about blocking
steps.stepSummary: רבא disagrees with רבי אילא. Since the משנה gives חציצה as the reason only in the last case, the first case must have a different reason.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Since the last clause is because of blocking, the first clause is not because of blocking.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא opens a new approach. He argues that the vessel-in-vessel case has nothing to do with חציצה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא reads the structure of the משנה. The משנה lists the knot case as its own separate rule, and that rule is the one about חציצה. So the first case, vessels inside vessels, must rest on a different reason.

phrases.aramaic: רָבָא אָמַר: מִדְּסֵיפָא הָוֵי מִשּׁוּם חֲצִיצָה,
phrases.english: Rava said: Since the last clause is because of blocking,
the first clause is not because of blocking.

steps.triggerLanguage: רָבָא אָמַר: מִדְּסֵיפָא הָוֵי מִשּׁוּם חֲצִיצָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רבי אילא's view that both cases are about חציצה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Immersing vessels inside vessels is forbidden for קודש for a reason other than חציצה.

steps.title: רבא's reason: a decree about needles in a narrow-mouthed vessel
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains that the first clause is a גזירה. It keeps people from immersing small items inside a vessel whose mouth is narrower than the tube of a wineskin.
steps.simpleTranslation: And this is the reason for the first clause: it is a decree so that a person will not immerse needles and hooks in a vessel whose opening is smaller than the tube of a wineskin.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא now gives his own reason for the first clause. It is a protective decree, not a rule about blocking.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a vessel's mouth is too narrow, the water inside it is not properly joined to the מקוה, so small items inside it are not really immersed. To keep people from making this mistake, the רבנן banned immersing vessels inside vessels for קודש altogether.

keyTerms.meaning: The tube or spout of a wineskin (a standard measure of width)

phrases.english: And as for the first clause, this is the reason:
it is a decree so that one will not immerse needles and hooks
in a vessel whose mouth is not as wide as the tube of a wineskin.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the positive reason behind רבא's claim in step 5.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Vessels inside vessels are forbidden for קודש as a גזירה, so that small items will not be immersed in a vessel with a mouth narrower than שפופרת הנוד.

steps.title: Source: the rule for joining ritual baths
steps.stepSummary: רבא supports his measure with a משנה. Two bodies of מקוה water count as joined only through an opening as wide as the tube of a wineskin.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned in a משנה: Ritual baths are joined through an opening the size of the tube of a wineskin, measured with its thickness...
steps.whatsHappening: רבא backs up his reason with a משנה that sets the measure for when water counts as connected to a מקוה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה shows that שפופרת הנוד is the minimum opening for two bodies of water to join. Water inside a vessel with a narrower mouth is therefore not joined to the מקוה, which is exactly the problem רבא's גזירה protects against. The quote continues on the next amud.

keyTerms.meaning: As we learned in a משנה
Joining bodies of water so they count as one מקוה

steps.whyThisMatters: This measure is what makes רבא's גזירה make sense. Without enough connection, the water inside the vessel does not count as part of the מקוה at all.

phrases.english: As we learned in a mishna: The joining of ritual baths
is through an opening the size of the tube of a wineskin, including its thickness

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for the שפופרת הנוד measure used in step 6.
steps.raayaObject: That water inside a vessel with a mouth narrower than שפופרת הנוד is not joined to the מקוה.
